ISSUE:
Modeling's `separability_matrix` does not compute separability correctly for nested CompoundModels
Consider the following model:

```python
from astropy.modeling import models as m
from astropy.modeling.separable import separability_matrix

cm = m.Linear1D(10) & m.Linear1D(5)
```

It's separability matrix as you might expect is a diagonal:

```python
>>> separability_matrix(cm)
array([[ True, False],
       [False,  True]])
```

If I make the model more complex:
```python
>>> separability_matrix(m.Pix2Sky_TAN() & m.Linear1D(10) & m.Linear1D(5))
array([[ True,  True, False, False],
       [ True,  True, False, False],
       [False, False,  True, False],
       [False, False, False,  True]])
```

The output matrix is again, as expected, the outputs and inputs to the linear models are separable and independent of each other.

If however, I nest these compound models:
```python
>>> separability_matrix(m.Pix2Sky_TAN() & cm)
array([[ True,  True, False, False],
       [ True,  True, False, False],
       [False, False,  True,  True],
       [False, False,  True,  True]])
```
Suddenly the inputs and outputs are no longer separable?

This feels like a bug to me, but I might be missing something?

I found the bug! In `_cstack`, when `right` is an ndarray (i.e., the result of a recursive `_separable` call on a nested CompoundModel), line 245 sets `cright[-right.shape[0]:, -right.shape[1]:] = 1` — it fills the block with all ones instead of using the actual values from `right`. This destroys the separability information of the nested model.

Let me verify by comparing with the `left` branch: when `left` is an ndarray, line 240 correctly copies `left` values: `cleft[: left.shape[0], : left.shape[1]] = left`. But for `right`, it incorrectly uses `= 1` instead of `= right`.

<policy_id>P2.2</policy_id>
<policy_action>compare</policy_action>

This explains the divergence: for the flat model `Pix2Sky_TAN() & Linear1D(10) & Linear1D(5)`, the `&` operator is left-associative, so it becomes `(Pix2Sky_TAN() & Linear1D(10)) & Linear1D(5)`. The right operand `Linear1D(5)` is always a `Model` instance (not an ndarray), so `_coord_matrix` is called correctly. But for the nested `Pix2Sky_TAN() & cm`, the right operand `cm` is a CompoundModel, so `_separable(cm)` returns an ndarray — and then `_cstack` incorrectly fills it with all ones.

def test_separability_matrix_nested_compound_model():
    """Regression test for nested CompoundModels separability matrix.

    Checks that separability_matrix correctly computes block-diagonal structure
    when a CompoundModel operand is itself a CompoundModel (nested case).
    See https://github.com/astropy/astropy/issues/XXXX
    """
    # A simple compound model (diagonal separability matrix)
    cm = models.Linear1D(10) & models.Linear1D(5)
    assert_allclose(separability_matrix(cm),
                    np.array([[True, False],
                              [False, True]]))

    # Flat compound: Pix2Sky_TAN() & Linear1D(10) & Linear1D(5)
    flat = models.Pix2Sky_TAN() & models.Linear1D(10) & models.Linear1D(5)
    expected = np.array([[True,  True, False, False],
                         [True,  True, False, False],
                         [False, False, True,  False],
                         [False, False, False, True]])
    assert_allclose(separability_matrix(flat), expected)

    # Nested compound: Pix2Sky_TAN() & (Linear1D(10) & Linear1D(5))
    # Should produce the same result as the flat form
    nested = models.Pix2Sky_TAN() & cm
    assert_allclose(separability_matrix(nested), expected)

    # Doubly nested: (Linear1D(10) & Linear1D(5)) & (Linear1D(10) & Linear1D(5))
    cm2 = models.Linear1D(10) & models.Linear1D(5)
    double_nested = cm & cm2
    expected_double = np.array([[True,  False, False, False],
                                [False, True,  False, False],
                                [False, False, True,  False],
                                [False, False, False, True]])
    assert_allclose(separability_matrix(double_nested), expected_double)
